exceptions.reason: This hook rides Claude Code's plan-mode completion signal (ExitPlanMode), which Codex has no equivalent for, so it cannot be registered there. What it DOES is no longer what this entry once recorded: it imports the accepted plan into the Project Manager as an unapproved draft, and it does not enter Build on either runtime. The Codex side is not left without the capability — the same import runs there through the typed acceptance envelope on UserPromptSubmit (see the plan-import-hook entry below), which is why this asymmetry is one of SIGNAL, not of function. Build entry stays the typed $engine-start on both runtimes; importing a draft grants no Build authority, so nothing here infers build intent from an acceptance.

The mirror of the entry above, and the reason that one is not a capability gap. Codex exposes no plan-exit completion, so its native-plan import is keyed on the acceptance envelope the operator types, read by a UserPromptSubmit owner registered after boot's per-prompt scent. Claude does not carry this registration because it does not need it: acceptance there arrives as a plan-exit completion and is already handled on PostToolUse. Registering both on Claude would give one event two importers of the same document — a duplicate-writer shape, and the second import would mint a second plan id for one accepted plan.

Claude Code pulls the codes of conduct into every session mechanically (the floor's @import); Codex has no import mechanism, so the AGENTS.md floor carries an imperative required-reading instruction instead — discipline where Claude has mechanics. The session-start briefing (when hooks run) independently carries the orientation, so the instruction is the fallback path, not the only one.

Live qualification on macOS with Codex CLI 0.153.4 (2026-09-08) confirmed that the same custom agent requested read-only, retained its configured model/effort, and inherited the parent task's effective sandbox. A Read Only child could invoke a shell but could not write the fixture file; a Workspace Write child wrote it. The Codex agent format has no per-tool denylist, so reviewer no-shell/no-write instructions remain discipline. Generated reviewers retain the read-only request, the strongest tested default, but it is not mechanical isolation from a Workspace Write parent. CLI evidence does not qualify Desktop. See codex-validation.md; repeat qualification if platform behavior changes.

Codex skips new or changed project hooks until the operator re-trusts them, so every engine update that touches the hook registration turns the engine's local guardrails OFF until /hooks re-approval. The engine says so at the moment it changes the registration; the status readout additionally warns when NO session in this project has run its hooks recently (a coarse net — a recent session on either runtime clears it for up to a day); and the per-session check is the floor's own grounding rule: verify the start-of-session briefing arrived, and treat the gates as off when it did not. Disclosure at three ranges, because no mechanism can re-trust on the operator's behalf.

The engine's two helper servers are registered on Codex with every tool auto-approved. The memory server now exposes six operations, three of which WRITE on the operator's say-so — pin, withhold and restore, beside the reads list-pins and list-withheld — so on Codex a model can save a standing note or take one out of recall without a fresh consent moment, where the Claude side records approval per tool and would prompt. Weighed and accepted as bounded rather than removed: all three append to the ledger and none deletes, withholding is reversed by restore, and permanent erasure stays behind a merged single-purpose pull request no tool here can reach. The wiring map's server remains read-only. The grant is still standing, so any FURTHER tool — in particular anything that removes rather than appends — must revisit this entry and the approval mode together.

Codex's own documentation states its pre-tool hook is a guardrail rather than a complete enforcement boundary, and that interception of its newer shell path is incomplete — so the Explore write-gate on Codex can miss shell forms the platform does not surface. The protected main branch and the operator's merge remain the only wall, on every runtime.

L4-9 live CLI 0.153.4 probes verified custom model/effort binding and an observable spawn hook, so neither a missing model field nor an absent spawn surface explains this omission anymore. A prose prohibition on recursive delegation does not prove mechanical leaf isolation; no recursion ceiling was established by these probes. The model and observation prerequisites are now available, while a supported scout permission/leaf-lock contract still needs the separately scoped #1075 decision. The Codex render remains omitted pending separate #1075 rollout. L4-9 verified custom model/effort binding, removing the former model-selection blocker. The runner must copy the entire working tree into disposable scratch before executing code. Under a Read Only parent that scratch write is blocked; under a Workspace Write parent the child can write, but its read-only request does not independently protect the source checkout. Codex has no per-tool denylist or proven mechanical leaf-lock for this role. A supported source-read-only/scratch-writable containment recipe remains unqualified, so an explicit integrator-created disposable copy is the available validation route; running tests in the live source as a substitute is not. CLI evidence does not qualify Desktop. No runner rollout is implied.

The spawn gate now runs on qualified Codex Agent/spawn spellings and gates the recognized native explorer role using explicit model input. The remaining matcher asymmetry is deliberate: Codex has no qualified native Plan role or equivalent in-session ScheduleWakeup scheduler. No scheduler spelling is invented or registered. The standing no-self-wakeup instruction remains on both runtimes; future role or scheduler support requires fresh qualification. Unknown launch shapes remain unclassified and allowed, never certified compliant.
